question: How does oxygen redox contribute to the capacity of battery cathodes?
answer: Oxygen redox contributes to cathode capacity by allowing oxide anions (O²⁻) to donate electrons during charging, thereby acting as reducing agents that compensate for the absence of oxidizable transition metals; this "may allow greater energy storage capacity in battery electrodes than would otherwise be theoretically predicted" (`...__k03.md`). The retrieved abstract chunk likewise states that "the participation of oxygen or other anionic species in redox activities in cathode materials for lithium and sodium-ion battery systems is known to play a role in governing the useful capacity of these batteries" (`...__k00.md`). The summary chunk adds that oxygen redox "was discovered to significantly contribute toward the overall battery capacity in Li-excess disordered spinel-type cathodes," with the extent varying by crystal structure and transition-metal type (`...__k23.md`, and its duplicate `...__k22.md`). A related chunk notes that actual cathodes can deliver "an overcapacity exceeding the transition metal oxidation limit," motivating investigation of anionic participation (`...__k01.md`).
